content: 1. Bedaquiline's metabolism is influenced by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Drugs that inhibit or induce this enzyme can alter bedaquiline's levels or effects. Avoid or consider alternative drugs in such cases. 2. Chloroquine increases the risk of bedaquiline toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 3. Chlorpromazine and bedaquiline both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring, including ECG, is recommended. 4. Ciprofloxacin, citalopram, and clarithromycin also increase the QTc interval when used with bedaquiline. Therapy adjustments and close ECG monitoring are necessary. 5. Clarithromycin can elevate bedaquiline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should not be coadministered with bedaquiline for more than 14 consecutive days unless the benefits outweigh the risks. 7. Clomipramine, clozapine, and other drugs that prolong the QTc interval require therapy modification and close ECG monitoring when used with bedaquiline. 8. Cobicistat and conivaptan increase bedaquiline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. Crizotinib and crofelemer also interact with bedaquiline, requiring caution and close monitoring. Crofelemer minimally inhibits CYP3A4 systemically but may affect gut concentrations. 10. Cyclophosphamide and danazol may increase bedaquiline levels, but the clinical significance is unclear. Monitor closely. 11. Dabrafenib decreases bedaquiline levels by inducing CYP3A4. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is advised. 12. Darunavir and dexamethasone affect bedaquiline metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 13. Dasatinib, degarelix, and desipramine prolong the QTc interval when combined with bedaquiline. Therapy adjustments and ECG monitoring are required. 14. Deutetrabenazine minimally prolongs the QT interval but may increase the risk of torsades de pointes under certain conditions. Use caution and monitor. 15. Drugs like disopyramide, dofetilide, dolasetron, and donepezil also increase the QTc interval with bedaquiline. Avoid or modify therapy and monitor ECG closely. 16. Dronedarone, droperidol, and other QTc-prolonging drugs require therapy modification and close monitoring when used with bedaquiline. 17. Efavirenz decreases bedaquiline levels by inducing CYP3A4 and also prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 18. Elagolix weakly induces CYP3A4 and may reduce bedaquiline levels. Monitor closely and adjust doses of CYP3A4 substrates if needed. 19. Eliglustat, elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF, and other strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase bedaquiline levels and prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 20. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 and prolongs the QTc interval with bedaquiline. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 21. Entrectinib, enzalutamide, and eribulin also interact with bedaquiline, requiring avoidance or alternative therapies. 22. Erythromycin (in various forms) and escitalopram prolong the QTc interval with bedaquiline. Therapy adjustments and ECG monitoring are necessary. 23. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases bedaquiline levels by inducing CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 24. Etravirine reduces bedaquiline levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 25. Ezogabine, fedratinib, and fexinidazole interact with bedaquiline, requiring caution, therapy modification, or avoidance. 26. Fingolimod, flecainide, and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval with bedaquiline. Therapy adjustments and ECG monitoring are required. 27. Fluoxetine, fluphenazine, and formoterol also increase the QTc interval with bedaquiline. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 28. Fosamprenavir and foscarnet interact with bedaquiline, requiring avoidance or close monitoring. 29. Fosphenytoin decreases bedaquiline levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 30. Fostemsavir, gadobenate, and gemifloxacin prolong the QTc interval with bedaquiline. Therapy adjustments and ECG monitoring are necessary. 31. Gemtuzumab, gepirone, and gilteritinib also interact with bedaquiline, requiring avoidance or alternative therapies. 32. Glasdegib and goserelin increase the risk of QTc prolongation and torsades de pointes with bedaquiline. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Granisetron, haloperidol, and histrelin prolong the QTc interval with bedaquiline. Therapy adjustments and ECG monitoring are required. 34. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and hydroxyzine also increase the QTc interval with bedaquiline. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 35. Ibutilide, idelalisib, and iloperidone interact with bedaquiline, requiring therapy modification or avoidance. 36. Imatinib, indapamide, and indinavir increase bedaquiline levels or prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 37. Inotuzumab, isoflurane, and isoniazid also interact with bedaquiline, requiring avoidance or close monitoring. 38. Isradipine, istradefylline, and itraconazole prolong the QTc interval or increase bedaquiline levels. Avoid or modify therapy and monitor closely. 39. Ivosidenib and ketoconazole interact with bedaquiline, requiring avoidance or alternative therapies. 40. Lapatinib, larotrectinib, and lefamulin also interact with bedaquiline, requiring therapy modification or avoidance. 41. Lenvatinib, leuprolide, and levalbuterol prolong the QTc interval with bedaquiline. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Levofloxacin, levoketoconazole, and lithium also interact with bedaquiline, requiring therapy modification or avoidance. 43. Lofexidine, lonafarnib, and loperamide increase the QTc interval with bedaquiline. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 44. Lopinavir, lorlatinib, and lumefantrine interact with bedaquiline, requiring therapy modification or avoidance. 45. Macimorelin, maprotiline, and mavorixafor prolong the QTc interval with bedaquiline. Therapy adjustments and ECG monitoring are necessary. 46. Mefloquine, methadone, and midostaurin also interact with bedaquiline, requiring therapy modification or avoidance. 47. Mifepristone, mirtazapine, and mitotane interact with bedaquiline, requiring therapy modification or avoidance. 48. Moxifloxacin, nafcillin, and nefazodone also interact with bedaquiline, requiring therapy modification or avoidance. 49. Nelfinavir, nevirapine, and nicardipine interact with bedaquiline, requiring therapy modification or avoidance. 50. Nilotinib, nirmatrelvir, and nirmatrelvir/ritonavir interact with bedaquiline, requiring therapy modification or avoidance. This list highlights the importance of monitoring QTc intervals and CYP3A4 interactions when coadministering bedaquiline with other drugs.
